Kingfisher: Keep a real compact-necked kingfisher; lift the head slightly so the short throat-to-breast connection is legible. Make both short leg roots and feet separately readable without lengthening its naturally short neck or tail.
Kiwi: Strictly face RIGHT, bill extending right from the small head. Keep the round tailless shaggy kiwi body and truly hidden wings; separate both stout short legs at their true roots. No invented tail, wing, neck or extra limbs.
Ostrich: Preserve the real long bare neck, tiny head and black-white plumes. Keep all feather masses connected to torso and expose both genuine leg roots, knees, ankles and two-toed feet in a separated shallow stride at equal foot level.
Owl: Keep a true short-necked barrel owl with attached feather tufts. Make the two feathered legs and complete feet separate and on the same level; keep folded wings and short true tail joined smoothly to the body, no isolated feather spikes.
Peacock: Keep the natural long eyespotted train continuously attached behind folded wings. Both real leg shafts must be fully readable from their body roots to spread toes with two separate equal-level feet. Never trade the long train for a short tail.
Pelican: Keep the huge bill and attached throat pouch, natural kinked neck and short legs. Show the neck root joining the shoulder smoothly, two separately readable short legs with broad webbed feet on the same level, and a compact attached crown without loose plume islands.
Pheasant: Retain the white neck ring, red facial patch and long barred tail. Separate both natural leg roots from the feathered belly through knees and ankles; keep two complete feet at the same level, without extending a thigh into an invented limb.
Quetzal: Retain both long green tail coverts, red belly and compact bristly crown. Both true short legs must emerge separately at their genuine roots and both complete feet end on exactly the same horizontal level. Keep streamers apart from feet and continuously attached.
Secretary Bird: Keep all true quill crest feathers visibly rooted in the head; no detached quill fragment. Preserve long crane-like legs, expose their real upper roots separately under belly, and retain a complete continuous tail and folded wings.
Swift: The first painting read as a generic long-legged perched bird. Paint a true swift with almost invisible extremely short cling-feet and long stiff folded sickle-wing tips projecting behind the cigar body, a short shallow-notched tail and tiny bill. Do not invent long walking legs or swallow streamers. Keep side-profile facing right and both true feet readable.
Tern: Retain a true tern with black cap, dagger bill, pointed folded wings and deeply forked tail. Separate the two natural short leg roots cleanly from belly and wings and make both feet individually readable at equal level; no crossing through the fixed torso region.
Tropicbird: Retain long paired tail streamers and black eye wedge. Both short legs must have distinct true body attachments and separate complete feet at the same level; do not merge a leg shaft into the streamers or folded wing.
Amphipod: Preserve a real laterally compressed C-curled gammarid amphipod, not a prawn or insect. Keep two pairs of antennae clearly separated at their true small head roots and distinguish genuine differently shaped underside limb groups and complete rear uropods. Do not add an insect waist or prawn tail fan.
Brine Shrimp: Preserve the shell-less slender Artemia tube, two stalked eyes and eleven pairs of real leaf-like paddles. Make the narrow rear abdomen and natural two-branched tail tips complete and separately readable from paddle limbs; never add a prawn carapace or replace leaf paddles with walking legs.
Cave Shrimp: Keep the glassy colourless cave shrimp, truly curved abdomen, complete tail fan and very long attached antennae. Show genuine near/far walking legs separately at their real trunk roots without merging them into antennae, and use a reduced unobtrusive eye region consistent with the canonical hidden-eye presentation.
Copepod: Keep a real calanoid copepod, with one simple median eye rather than paired stalked eyes. Show two long true antennules, the teardrop front body, natural paddle legs, narrow segmented rear abdomen and forked bristly tail at their correct separate attachments. No invented prawn legs or giant tail fan.
Fairy Shrimp: Keep a true shell-less fairy shrimp with eleven pairs of leaf-like swimming paddles and stalked eyes. Separate the front feelers, paddle roots and natural narrow abdomen/tail fork while retaining true proportions; no carapace, pincers or invented walking feet.
Freshwater Shrimp: The first painting had oversized crayfish-like claws. Keep only tiny slender forceps on the true front legs, with ordinary shrimp walking legs clearly separated behind them, very long attached antennae, a curved segmented abdomen and complete tail fan. No thick lobster or crayfish pincers.
Giant Isopod: Keep the real overlapping pill-bug armour and seven pairs of true walking legs, not insect anatomy. Clearly show both genuine antenna pairs including the small antennules, attached to the compact head, and natural rear uropods. No prawn tail fan or extra walking leg pairs.
Isopod: Preserve seven pairs of true similar legs and overlapping flattened body plates. Separate visible near/far feet without adding pairs; show the two natural rear uropods beside the rear plate and attached head antennae. Never replace uropods with a giant prawn fan.
Krill: Keep the real translucent krill with external feathery gills, large stalked black eyes and no large claws. Show all naturally visible near/far trunk limbs and swimming legs attached individually, separated from antennae and complete tail fan; no floating detached limb island.
Shrimp: Retain true shrimp anatomy: small head, serrated rostrum, attached long antennae, curved segmented abdomen and complete tail fan. Separate genuine near/far walking leg roots and feet and keep every limb attached, without adding a large claw or detached appendage.
Tadpole Shrimp: Keep the broad true Triops shield, close dorsal eyes, many leaf legs and exactly two long thin tail filaments. Make the real rear segmented body, leg fringes and anterior sensing appendages distinct at true attachments. Do not force prawn walking legs, stalked eyes or a broad prawn tail fan onto it.
Vent Shrimp: Preserve the arched translucent vent-shrimp body and pale dorsal light-sensing patch, without stalked eyes. Use small slender feeding claws, clearly separated real near/far walking limbs and long sweeping antennae; keep tail fan and all antenna/leg roots continuously attached.
Water Flea: Keep a true Daphnia: transparent tall teardrop shell, visible gut and brood chamber, one large eye and two large branched rowing antennae. Make the genuine internal filter limbs and natural posterior spine readable. Never invent prawn walking legs, a long prawn abdomen or a large tail fan to match another species.
Kookaburra: The latest original was anatomy ADMIT but static intake refused: observed surfaces contact conflicts with fixed owner. Keep the large dagger bill and eye stripe, but paint one smooth continuous nape joined to its own neck, with compact rooted feathers and no stray back-of-head spike. Separate both feet naturally without crossing or fusing their roots. This is a new source composition, not permission to weaken the splitter or compression limits.
